### §6 PROPOSAL — reducing repetitive authorization friction (evidence-backed; NO protocol change in this mission)
The breach above had ONE root cause: no WORK_ITEM_CONTRACT was authored before executing (protocol workflow step 3/4 skipped). A proposal to cut approval round-trips WITHOUT weakening control, classifying each action type by the authorization it actually needs:
- **(a) Already covered by a valid contract** — any action whose file ∈ the contract `write_set` and whose effect ∈ `allowed_commands`. Needs NO further approval; just execute + record evidence. *Evidence:* this mission's 6-file edits + focused tests are all inside the authorized contract.
- **(b) Routine steps implicit in an authorized objective** — read-only inspection, focused/affected tests, typecheck, dual-port parity, and a fingerprint-gated guarded build that SKIPs when inputs are unchanged. These are verification, not new effects; they should be pre-included by any contract whose `acceptance_criteria` cite them. *Evidence:* Gates 1–4 here produced zero new side effects (build SKIPped).
- **(c) Bounded recovery permitted within the contract** — rollback via `git checkout -- <write_set>` + guarded rebuild, explicitly named in the contract `rollback` field. No fresh approval needed to restore to the contracted baseline. *Evidence:* contract `rollback` is self-contained and touches only the write-set.
- **(d) Genuinely needs FRESH human approval** — PROPOSED→AUTHORIZED of a NEW work item; any write outside `write_set`; a new security boundary (e.g. wiring the canonical runtime queue into the runner); systemd/timer/env/allowlist/ledger/audit/Truth-Lock changes; mission dispatch/provider calls; reboot; commit to a protected path; push/RELEASE. These stay human-gated.

**Recommendation (for a SEPARATE reviewed plan, not executed here):** make contract authoring the mandatory *first* step of any campaign so (a)–(c) run without round-trips while (d) stays gated; optionally add a tiny read-only `odg contract status <id>` check so a provider can prove (a)/(b)/(c) coverage before acting. This changes workflow discipline, not the authorization policy.

Entry via compass. Truth Lock: branched off origin/main bb14bc0 (Go lot = branch excellence/go-build-capability, PR#170

**Defect demonstrated (code):** campaign-controller had NO no-repeat/attempt/fingerprint logic. A READY lot that fails
is re-selected identically forever — BEFORE: selectNextLot over [A(fails),B] returned ["A","A","A","A"] (B starved,

lot where lastFailureFingerprint===current fingerprint (isStalled) ⇒ not re-selected while unchanged; a new strategy/
inputsHash (or clearFailure, e.g. new evidence) changes the fingerprint ⇒ re-admitted. summary surfaces stalled[].
AFTER: ["A","B",null,null]; A strategy-change ⇒ A selectable again. Backward-compatible (existing items have no
lastFailureFingerprint ⇒ unaffected; real register 0 stalled).

fingerprint determinism+sensitivity). Gate: test:report 176, tsc 0, build 0. €0. Blockers unchanged (5 external).

Truth Lock at start: main @ f4d6e45 == origin/main (div 0/0), clean modulo the uncommitted handoff checkpoint (now committed WITH this lot). Safe-resume done: fetch-not-blind-pull, compass preserved. 5 stashes / 1 worktree / 4 branches intact.

PURE PARSE, NO network/fetch/crawl/DNS; fail-closed (bad input⇒structured error, absent⇒null); nothing published; no ranking claim. robots.txt grounded on the OFFICIAL Google spec (verified via WebSearch 2026-10-30, cited): most-specific (longest) UA group wins + specific/`*` never combined; rule precedence = longest rule path wins, Allow wins ties; `*`/`$` wildcards; empty Disallow⇒allow-all; Sitemap directives global. isPathAllowed = robots CRAWL decision (explicitly distinct from meta-robots INDEX). sitemap.xml grounded on sitemaps.org 0.9: urlset(loc/lastmod/changefreq/priority) + sitemapindex(loc/lastmod), structural validation (loc absolute http(s), priority∈[0,1], changefreq enum, lastmod W3C-datetime) as SARIF findings — never fabricates validity; nested sitemaps LISTED not fetched.
INDEPENDENT AUDIT (general-purpose sonnet, ran counterexamples) caught 2 REAL HIGH defects — BOTH FIXED + regression-tested:
  (F1 false-readiness) group selection filtered `specificAgentMatch>=0` (ANY matching UA token) instead of `===bestSpecific` (ONLY the single most-specific). A less-specific sibling token (`Bot` vs `Botxyz`) wrongly merged its Allow ⇒ a disallowed page reported crawl-ALLOWED. FIX: filter `===bestSpecific`. Proven: Botxyz ⇒ allowed:false (was true). Real-world trigger: Googlebot/Googlebot-Image, Yandex/YandexBot siblings.
  (F2 DoS) sitemap block extraction used a global lazy `[\s\S]*?` regex = QUADRATIC on many-opens/no-close input (measured 17.2s@500KB; ~75min extrapolated at the 8MB bound). FIX: replaced with a LINEAR indexOf-based extractElementBlocks (boundary-checked so <urlset>/</sitemapindex> never false-match <url>/</sitemap>; stops when no further close exists). Proven: 500KB 17.2s→22ms. Auditor independently VERIFIED correct: regex escaping, precedence once-correct-set, default-allow honesty, no-network, no-fabrication, no-throw.
  Minor (documented, non-blocking): userAgent contract = bare product token; percent-encoding not normalised across rule↔URL (KNOWN LIMITATION in doc).
Gate: tsc 0, build 0 (dist closure 118), targeted 18/18, full regression 206/206 (0 fail, 0 stale). §8 SEO workstream now: seo-strategy + seo-technical-audit + seo-page-signal-extractor + seo-crawl-directives — all local, nothing published, no ranking claim.
Register: unchanged pending PR merge (will be 71 ACCEPTED). LESSON: a robots.txt group selector MUST bind to the SINGLE most-specific UA (===bestSpecific), not any-prefix-match, or a sibling token's Allow leaks a false crawl-permission; HTML/XML block extraction with an unbounded lazy quantifier is quadratic even under a byte cap — use a linear indexOf scanner that halts when no closing tag remains.

ROOT CAUSE: the guard treated ANY negation word anywhere in the clause as suppressing the effect, incl. WEAK adverbials (no/without/sans/sauf) that often don't scope the verb ⇒ 'without further delay delete the production database' / 'no backup so wipe' / 'sans hesitation supprime' downgraded to NONE/LOW/no-human. Non-adjacent weak ⇒ effect stands (fail-closed). Also GATED nl-objective-gateway.test.ts into test:report (the classifier's own test was ungated). +case 29.

LESSON (important): "adding clause boundaries only shortens the clause ⇒ strictly safer" is FALSE for a STRONG negator — a boundary (connector OR comma) BETWEEN the negator and its verb strips the prohibition from the signal's clause ⇒ catastrophic INVERSION. Independent audit caught what my own safety-argument missed — treat a plausible monotonicity claim as a hypothesis to disprove, not a proof.
HONEST RESIDUAL FAIL-OPENS (documented, NOT fixed — each a dedicated future lot; code NOTE added in test 29): F1/F6 strong-negator scope across an interjection (connector/comma aside) can invert a prohibition ('do not, under any circumstances, delete X'⇒DESTRUCTIVE — PRE-EXISTING, commas were already boundaries; the MORE severe of the two directions, natural phrasing); F2 bare ne/pas FR-token collision in EN text; F3 Arabic لكن connector gap; F4 O(n^2) when every signal is adjacently negated (availability).
